title: dedicated-autoscaler-fleet-util-reporting-burst-controls-improvement
author: Daniel Lee
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleet autoscaler has been allowing short bursts that exceed throughput guarantees under priority routing, causing uneven tail latency and confusing utilization reporting. This PR improves burst controls and enriches utilization reporting so operators can (1) enforce throughput guarantees more predictably, (2) observe burst consumption across priority classes, and (3) debug regressions faster.

Summary of changes: implemented a token-bucket smoothing layer for burst allowance with configurable smoothing window; integrated burst accounting into per-priority utilization metrics; added new Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboards; surfaced burst/headroom fields in the DedicatedFleet API and console; added unit and integration tests for burst depletion/restore scenarios; improved autoscaler documentation and rollout playbook.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc linked (ENG-4123)
- [x] Unit tests for tokenbucket smoothing
- [x] Integration tests exercising priority routing under burst
- [x] End-to-end canary plan added to rollout notes
- [x] Updated console UI to show per-priority burst headroom

Behavioral notes (backwards compatibility): default smoothing window is 60s and default burst allowance remains at previous configured values to avoid sudden impacts. Operators can opt into the new smoothing algorithm via feature flag default-enabled for newly created fleets; existing fleets will be migrated to the new behavior over a 2-week rollout window with an opt-out. API changes are additive (new optional fields) and do not break existing clients.

Testing & CI: local unit tests and the dedicated-integration pipeline were run. The first CI run hit a flaky end-to-end test (queueing_backpressure_test) and was retriggered; subsequent runs passed. Load testing on a 10-node dedicated fleet using synthetic traffic validated improved tail latency (p95 down ~18%) and reduced burst-induced overcommit events by ~62% compared to baseline.

Rollout plan: staged canary (5% fleets -> 25% -> 100%) with monitoring alerts for increased request rejection or unexpected throttles; automated rollback runbook included. Console flag and Linear playbook reference included in PR.

Related work: builds on prior reporting improvements in ENG-3984 and ties into the throughput guarantee refactor (ENG-4007).

Notes for reviewers: key areas to inspect are the tokenbucket implementation (autoscaler/service/tokenbucket.go) for correctness under concurrent drains, the prometheus metric naming/labels to ensure cardinality control, and the migration path in api/v1/fleet_config.proto.

Release notes: Improved dedicated autoscaler burst smoothing and utilization reporting; owners can enable improved smoothing to reduce transient capacity overcommit and gain finer-grained per-priority burst metrics.

review_comments: Priya Patel: Nice. Please double-check locking around the tokenbucket refill path - I think there's a subtle race if OnDemandScale() triggers while refill is in-flight.
Daniel Lee (author): Good catch - added a per-bucket mutex and test that simulates concurrent drain/refill. See tokenbucket_test.go commit.
Anita Rao: Can we keep metric cardinality low? Suggest using 'priority' label with a small enum rather than full route ids.
Daniel Lee (author): Updated metrics to use priority enum and added a comment explaining the trade-off. Also added a tag to avoid high-cardinality labels in the console telemetry aggregation.
Samira Khan: Integration test looks flakey in CI due to timing. Recommend increasing the default smoothing window in test to make it deterministic.
Daniel Lee (author): Increased smoothing window in integration test and added explicit time control mocks to make behavior deterministic.
